theorem: For every integer s>=1 and r>=0 there exists chi_s(r) in {0,1} such that J_C_s(r)=J_N(r)-chi_s(r).
equivalent_shell_form: M_C_s(r) in {M_N(r), M_N(r)-1}; when J_N(r)=0, M_C_s(r)=M_N(r)=r.
no_ahead_proof: If N rejects shell m then Q(c_m)>r^2. Every microcentroid z with Q(z)<=r^2 must lie strictly in the inward Q-tangent halfspace at c_m. The exact tangent-count lemma puts fewer than s^2/2 samples there, so C_s cannot select shell m. Hence M_C_s<=M_N.
at_most_one_delay_proof: If J_N>0, N accepts c_{M_N}; the complete preceding limiting triangle T_{M_N-1} lies inside Q<=Q(c_{M_N})<=r^2, hence every one of its s^2 samples is inside and C_s accepts M_N-1. If J_N=0, T_r itself is wholly inside. Hence M_C_s>=M_N-1.
delay_bit: chi_s(r)=1 iff 2*K_s(r,M_N(r))<s^2; otherwise chi_s(r)=0. Exact half ties have chi=0 by the inherited AD >= rule.
sampling_uniformity: the phase bound needs no s0; it is uniform over the entire finite-sampling family s>=1
resolver_selection: NOT implied: the theorem proves bounded phase/asymptotic robustness, not that N and C are identical or that one is uniquely canonical
